    Am J Clin Nutr
    Adoption and utilization trends of a new diagnosis code for pediatric intestinal failure: a multicenter retrospective cross-sectional database analysis.
Adoption of the IF diagnosis code increases gradually. Although clinically coherent, incomplete adoption likely underestimates the true disease burden. Even when identified solely by diagnosis code, pediatric IF is associated with substantial inpatient morbidity and cost.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Associations of Dietary Patterns with Dementia Burden and Environmental Footprints among Older Adults: A Country-Level Longitudinal Ecological Analysis of 185 Countries and Territories, 1990-2018.
In this country-level ecological analysis, mPHDI showed the clearest health and environmental alignment, being associated with a lower dementia DALY rate, GHG emissions and land use, but greater water scarcity. These findings may inform context-specific policies considering healthy aging and environmental sustainability.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Circulating levels of glucoselysine, a fructose-specific glycation product, are modulated by dietary fructose: post hoc analysis of a case-control study and a randomized controlled trial.
Total serum GL can be analyzed accurately and precisely using UPLC-MS/MS. Our findings from 2 clinical studies demonstrate that GL formation is significantly influenced by dietary fructose intake. The observation that GL levels were not completely reduced after dietary fructose restriction suggests that additional factors, such as an endogenous fructose pool, contribute to GL formation. Further research is needed to elucidate the role of GL formation in fructose-induced cardiometabolic complications.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Dietary supplementation with plant sterols for obesity management and related metabolic disorders: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover clinical trial.
 In individuals with overweight or class I-III obesity, 2 g/day of PS did not reduce LDL-cholesterol compared with placebo, and no effect was found on any other cardiometabolic parameter. This may reflect reduced PS efficacy in this population. The trial was powered only for LDL-C and therefore, the secondary findings are exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered trials. Clinical trial registration
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Differential effects of stearic, palmitic, and oleic acid-enriched diets on gut microbiome, bile acid, and cholesterol metabolism in mildly hypercholesterolemic postmenopausal females: A secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
The cholesterol-lowering effects of 18 0 and 18 1 relative to 16 0 involved shared hepatic regulation of BA and cholesterol metabolism, whereas 18 0 uniquely modulated specific microbial taxa and BAs, suggestive of altered enterohepatic BA recycling.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Dynamic association between breastfeeding and weight retention within the first year postpartum: A trajectory analysis study based on the China multicentre mother-infant cohort.
 Early exclusive breastfeeding and greater cumulative breastfeeding exposure were strongly associated with favorable maternal weight trajectories. Low early breastfeeding predisposition/state highlighted an early intervention window for SPPWR. The CBI may serve as a preliminary cumulative exposure indicator in this Chinese cohort.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Effect of diarrhea on early-life gut microbiome composition and subsequent infant growth in Beira, Mozambique: analysis of the PAASIM longitudinal birth cohort.
These findings suggest that early microbial trajectories, independent of cumulative diarrheal burden, may be linked to growth outcomes, warranting further research to identify potential microbiome-targeted interventions in the first year of life, a pivotal window for promotion of healthy growth in resource-limited settings.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Evaluation of antenatal multiple micronutrient versus iron and folic acid supplementation in UNRWA health clinics serving Palestine refugees in Jordan: A systems trial.
MMS outperformed IFA on adherence, acceptability, side effects, mid-pregnancy anemia prevention, and use of system resources.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Exploring Socioeconomic Disparities: The Association between the Mediterranean Lifestyle and Mortality across Education and Income Levels in the Prospective Lifelines Cohort.
Higher adherence to the MEDLIFE index was linked to lower all-cause mortality across al socioeconomic levels, with income being the strongest modifier of this association. Poor lifestyle increased mortality similarly in adults with high and low education. Our findings suggest that healthy lifestyles could mitigate socioeconomic mortality gaps, promoting the Mediterranean lifestyle as an effective public health strategy.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Life-course associations of early-life risk factors, modifiable adult lifestyles, and transitions of cardiometabolic disease and multimorbidity: A prospective cohort study.
Joint exposure to adverse early-life experiences and an unhealthy adult lifestyle was associated with elevated risks of CMD progression and mortality. Notably, the detrimental associations of early-life risk factors with specific CMD transitions were less pronounced among individuals with healthier adult lifestyles.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Lifestyle determinants of glycemic responses to snacking in free-living adults without diabetes: an intensive longitudinal observational study.
Snack composition, snack timing, and postprandial physical activity were associated with postprandial glucose responses to snacking in adults without diabetes. Recommendations on snacking-related lifestyle behaviors may improve glycemic control in daily life.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Sex- and menopausal status-specific patterns of fat free mass loss and cardiorespiratory fitness after metabolic bariatric surgery: the Stratification of Obesity Phenotypes to Optimize Future Obesity Therapy (SOPHIA) longitudinal cohort.
FFM loss after MBS differs by sex and menopausal status  males and postmenopausal females lose a greater proportion of FFM relative to TWL than premenopausal females. Nevertheless, CRF improves across al groups, showing postoperative gains in CRF can occur despite FFM reductions. These findings highlight substantial interindividual variability in the composition of weight loss after MBS, which is not fully explained by biological sex, menopausal status, or baseline adiposity.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx The Impact of a Low Glycemic Load Breakfast on Diurnal Glucose Profiles in Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: The GLIDING Randomized Crossover Trial.
In women with GDM, an LGL-B was associated with lower breakfast PPG and 24-h %CV. Targeting breakfast may be a simple dietary strategy to improve glycemia and reduce morning bolus insulin requirements.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Inflamm Bowel Dis
    B cells regulate T cell transfer colitis by partially reconstituting luminal IgA and modulating the colonic microbiota.
Importantly, because IgA-deficient B cells failed to attenuate colitis despite comparable peripheral B cell reconstitution, these findings support an important role for IgA in mediating the protective effect of B cell transfer. Collectively, these findings identify IgA-mediated modulation of the microbiota as an alternate mechanism by which B cells attenuate T cell transfer colitis, highlighting a Breg-independent regulatory pathway with potential relevance to inflammatory bowel disease pathogenesis.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Current evidence for first-line advanced therapies in pediatric ulcerative colitis: a critical review.
Current pediatric evidence supports the efficacy of multiple advanced therapies and has characterized important safety outcomes;  however, evidence establishing therapeutic efficacy should be distinguished from evidence directly informing first-line treatment selection. Future pediatric research should increasingly generate comparative and predictive evidence that informs which effective advanced therapy should be selected first and for whom.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Endoscopic and histologic healing distribution and persistent rectosigmoiditis in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. 
Endoscopic improvement/remission and histologic remission were significantly more likely in the ascending and transverse colon than the rectum. Our findings demonstrate that endoscopic and histologic healing is more challenging in the rectum compared with proximal colonic segments.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Enterotype-based stratification identifies clinically distinct microbial subtypes in inflammatory bowel disease.
Gut microbial enterotypes are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes and treatment escalation in IBD, and exhibit enterotype-specific microbial community structures and alterations across disease states. Enterotype-based stratification may provide a clinically relevant framework for assessing risk assessment and guiding personalized disease management.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Health-related quality of life after diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease: 3-year trajectories and factors associated with clinically meaningful improvement (the IBSEN III cohort).
Clinically meaningful HRQoL improvement was achieved by about half of the patients and was consistently associated with lower symptom and psychosocial burden.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Large-scale proteomics identifies a pretreatment Crohn's disease core proteome and a dynamic signature for anti-TNF response.
In an exploratory investigation, we identified a CD Core Proteome and three-protein panel whose early changes were associated with M12 endoscopic remission, supporting their use as early pharmacodynamic response markers following external validation.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Morganella morganii-derived histamine impairs intestinal barrier function via HRH4 and aggravates colitis.
These findings suggest a previously unrecognized pathway in which the diet-responsive pathobiont M. morganii may impair epithelial barrier integrity through histamine-HRH4 signaling. Targeting histamine synthesis and HRH4 may offer a potential therapeutic avenue worth further investigation.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx J Crohns Colitis
    Building sustainable IBD clinical research units: a practical toolbox emerging from a Belgian multi-stakeholder initiative.
Beyond describing the toolbox, we discuss the concept of research readiness as a hallmark of excellence in modern IBD care and propose a roadmap for building sustainable research ecosystems. Although developed within the Belgian healthcare system, the principles presented are broadly applicable and may support the development of research capacity across healthcare systems and disease areas.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx   PMCChallenges and opportunities facing inflammatory bowel disease in Sub-Saharan Africa: towards a contextually relevant research and practice agenda.
In this viewpoint article we synthesize the challenges facing IBD in SSA and propose a research and practice agenda for addressing these, building on several promising initiatives already under way. Ultimately, we make a call to the international IBD community, researchers, funders, and policymakers to recognize the importance of IBD in SSA and join efforts to remedy global disparities in the quality, accessibility, and equity of IBD care.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Contemporary multicentre validation and comparative performance of Day 1 prognostic scores in acute severe ulcerative colitis.
 Day 1 prognostic scores demonstrate moderate performance in contemporary ASUC, with differing trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity. These findings support the use of Day 1 risk scores as adjuncts to early clinical decision-making in ASUC.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Epidemiology of inflammatory bowel disease in the Middle East and North Africa: a multinational, tertiary care registry (MIRAGE) study.
 This multi-country hospital-based registry study helps define contemporary IBD patterns in MENA  slight UC predominance, high rates of extensive UC and ileocolonic B1 CD, and heterogeneous biologic use. Our data provide insights into regional IBD epidemiological trends and treatment adoption.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Etrasimod reduces circulating and mucosal inflammatory lymphocyte populations and alters innate immune and non-immune cell signatures in intestinal mucosa: ELEVATE UC phase 3 clinical data.
Etrasimod treatment of patients with ulcerative colitis drives T- and B-lymphocyte subset reductions in blood and intestinal mucosa, neutrophil reductions in tissue and mucosal downregulation of inflammatory pathways associated with ulcerative colitis pathogenesis. Clinical trials registration number ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03945188;  NCT03996369).
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Plasma lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP), a proxy for intestinal permeability, relates to clinicopathological and immunological disease activity in inflammatory bowel disease patients at diagnosis and during disease course.
Plasma LBP relates to clinicopathological and immunological disease activity in IBD-especially UC-at diagnosis and during follow-up, and provides complementary information to routinely used blood-based biomarkers, arguing this simple, inexpensive parameter should be (re)considered for monitoring mucosal inflammation in UC.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Safety and tolerability of anti-toll-like receptor 3, monoclonal antibody PRV-300 in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis: a randomized phase 1B clinical trial (PULSE).
While PRV-300 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, TLR3 blockade did not translate into clinical benefit despite exploratory evidence of target engagement. Our results are challenging a pivotal role of the mode-of-action for the pathogenesis of UC (funded by Provention Bio). Clinical trial registration
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx   PMCTofacitinib 20 vs 30 mg in acute severe ulcerative colitis: a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
In this exploratory pilot trial, no statistically significant differences were observed with tofacitinib 30 mg/day compared with 20 mg/day when administered with IVCS. Clinical trial registration
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Liver Transpl
    Changing national practice patterns in living donor BMI and liver biopsy utilization from 2000-2024.
Donor and recipient BMI have both increased since 2000, yet donor obesity was not associated with inferior recipient outcomes. Liver biopsy utilization has declined substantially, with persistent regional and center-level variation. Standardization of steatosis assessment may help expand the living donor pool without compromising outcomes. Future studies should assess graft-specific outcomes and long-term steatosis recurrence.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx External validation of the SALT-M score in living donor liver transplantation for acute-on-chronic liver failure.
In LDLT-dominant ACLF cohorts - evaluated largely outside the severe-ACLF population for which SALT-M was derived - discrimination could not be confirmed, reflecting profound spectrum restriction and few outcome events rather than demonstrated model failure. SALT-M should be applied cautiously as an adjunctive risk-stratification tool, not as a universal threshold for transplant candidacy.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx External validation of the SNAPP score for hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence after living donor liver transplantation. 
SNAPP showed discrimination comparable to MoRAL and exceeded Milan, with numerically higher but not definitively superior discrimination compared with Metroticket 2.0, French-AFP, and three LDLT-specific selection systems, while resolving biologic heterogeneity within Milan-eligible candidates using only pretransplant variables. With near-zero calibration-in-the-large but a slope below unity, SNAPP supports risk stratification at listing, though individualized probability estimates require recalibration.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation; results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Recurrent primary sclerosing cholangitis after liver transplantation: Impact of inflammatory bowel disease on graft outcomes in a Southern European multicenter cohort.
Recurrent PSC was associated with impaired graft outcomes, including reduced graft survival and increased retransplantation. These findings highlight the importance of careful IBD monitoring after LT and support structured long-term surveillance strategies.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Pancreas
    Association between Serum Human Satellite II RNA and miR-21-5p Levels and Time to Pancreatic Cancer Diagnosis in a Prospective Population-based Study.
The PDAC index showed a possible association with proximity of pancreatic cancer diagnosis, with higher values observed closer to clinical diagnosis. While these preliminary findings should be interpreted in light of the study limitations, they provide a rationale for further evaluation of the PDAC index in larger studies with longer follow-up periods.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Care Gaps in Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy: A Survey of Real-World Practice Patterns in the United States.
 Real-world PERT prescribing for EPI in the U.S. frequently falls short of guideline-recommended dosing and follow-up is often delayed. Providing patients with instructions snack dosing and early reassessment represent gaps in EPI care, underscoring the importance of HCP training and education to optimize outcomes of EPI treatment.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Effects of Febuxostat, a Non-purine Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitor, on Cerulein-induced and L-Arginine-induced Acute Pancreatitis in Rats.
Our results suggest that XO inhibition alone does not have a therapeutic effect on AP and XO is not significantly involved in the progression of AP in either AP model.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Pancreatology
    Association of obstructive sleep apnea with pancreatic cancer in high-risk patients under surveillance in CAPS and PCYST cohorts.
Patients undergoing pancreatic surveillance for their familial/genetic risk and/or incidentally detected pancreatic cysts have a greater likelihood of developing pancreatic cancer if they've been diagnosed with OSA.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Pancreatic cancer cell and stellate cell-derived exosome crosstalk mediates pancreatic cancer-related diabetes.
 This study identifies a potential contributor to PCRD and suggests a possible mechanistic role for exosomal G6PD in impaired insulin signalling associated with PCRD.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Risk assessment of multi-focal side-branch IPMNs: Long-term follow-up of one thousand patients.
 Multiplicity of SB-IPMNs does not confer increased malignant risk at the patient level, despite nearly 40% of patients presenting with more than one cyst. These findings support a pancreas-wide susceptibility process (described as a "field defect") rather than a focal cyst-driven phenomenon. Accordingly, each cyst should be evaluated independently according to its own risk features.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx TRIM29 may facilitate progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma through immune remodeling.
 This study identifies TRIM29 as a machine learning-prioritized diagnostic biomarker and functional regulator of PDAC progression and immune remodeling, suggesting its potential value for biomarker-guided risk assessment and therapeutic exploration in PDAC.
Pubmed   Journal   ReadQx Utility of longitudinal changes in CA19-9 for detection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in patients with benign pancreatic diseases.
Longitudinal assessment of CA19-9 may support earlier detection of PDAC in patients with benign pancreatic diseases.
